Current research in microbial sciences 2026-12-01 Medium

Ultra-deep HiFi sequencing reveals rare structural-variant subpopulations in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from an LVAD-associated infection.

This study applies ultra-deep HiFi long-read sequencing to a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a left ventricular assist device (LVAD)-associated infection, revealing rare structural-variant subpopulations within the bacterial population. The work demonstrates that deep long-read sequencing can uncover within-host genomic heterogeneity that standard sequencing would miss, with implications for understanding antibiotic and phage resistance.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of tools that assess variants in isolation. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation for comprehensive genomic profiling in precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus classifications.

Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology 2026-11-12 Medium

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review discusses DNAzyme-based biosensors as a promising approach for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. The authors argue that these catalytic DNA sensors offer advantages over conventional genotyping methods by combining programmable nucleic acid recognition with catalytic signal amplification under isothermal conditions, potentially enabling accurate detection of low-abundance SNPs in complex biological samples with less sophisticated instrumentation.

Genome research 2026-11-10 Medium

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework for detecting viral genome variation directly from sequencing reads. It uses locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting to rapidly identify SNPs relative to reference genomes, avoiding the computational cost of traditional alignment-based pipelines. This enables scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets.

The Journal of infectious diseases 2026-11-10 Medium

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examines the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and finds that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the serotype 15A capsule, not just the previously recognized 15A and 15F forms. The work shows that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation differences that matter for vaccine serotype classification, including the proposed '15D' variant.

Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding.

This review examines how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to livestock genetics and breeding, noting that while animal breeding has long used data-driven prediction, modern AI approaches are still at an early stage. The authors survey current applications and highlight substantial potential for AI to improve selection and breeding decisions in milk, meat, and egg production.

Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.

This study systematically optimizes long-read metagenomic workflows for gut microbiome samples, from sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes. By integrating experimental and computational steps, the authors identify workflow configurations that yield better assembly contiguity and genome recovery than standard approaches.

Journal of proteome research 2026-11-06 Medium

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass glycosaminogalactan from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus that contains a rare pyruvylated GalNAcβ1→2Gal motif. Using proteomics-guided analysis of the strain grown on this substrate, they identified candidate CAZymes likely responsible for degrading this uncommon exopolysaccharide structure. This work expands knowledge of carbohydrate-active enzyme diversity and provides leads for enzymes acting on non-canonical EPS modifications.

Genome biology and evolution 2026-11-05 Medium

Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's reliance on self-fertile hermaphrodite species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from the androdioecious Elegans Group are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful outcrossing counterpart for comparative studies.

Molecular plant 2026-11-04 Medium

Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can be applied to predictive plant breeding across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and breeding design. The authors also conduct a systematic evidence audit of the field, highlighting gaps between claimed capabilities and demonstrated performance. The paper serves as a critical synthesis of both the promise and the current limitations of AI foundation models in crop improvement.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves Z-DNA-forming region detection by combining a permissive scan (high recall) with a stringent scan (high precision) and integrating the results through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan strategy addresses the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction, offering a fast and interpretable protocol.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments, following the principle of Mendelian randomization. Its key advance is the ability to robustly account for high-dimensional confounding variables—such as other genes, biological processes, and demographic factors—which existing methods struggle with. This enables more accurate causal network inference in genomic trio data.

Microbial genomics 2026-11-01 Medium

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by matching degenerate attachment site (att) patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap for researchers studying the diversity and mobility of these mobile genetic elements beyond just methicillin resistance.

Environmental microbiology 2026-11-01 Medium

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study tested whether bacterial metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from genome sequences alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors found that predictions for simple substrates were limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains incorrectly predicted. The work cautions against assuming genome-based metabolic inference is broadly reliable.

JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health 2026-11-01 Medium

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

This study used long-read sequencing to characterize the FLG gene, whose repetitive exon 3 has historically made variant detection difficult, in a diverse cohort of 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda. The authors identified extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detected both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. Long-read technology improved resolution of this challenging genomic region and enabled better detection of disease-relevant variants.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-10-31 Medium

Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a kidney-specific, cell-type-resolved manner, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and clinical conditions. This provides a practical template for adapting general S2F models to specialized tissues without training from scratch.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes linked to floatptosis, a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By combining single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and to features relevant to immunotherapy response.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect, as well as for in silico analysis of genomic AI models. It addresses the tedium and error-proneness of library design by providing purpose-built software, filling a gap where researchers previously relied on ad hoc scripts.

Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.

The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab, a free, community-supported web platform that packages over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible analysis of microbial omics data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers for microbiologists working with metabarcoding, metagenomic, and metatranscriptomic data while promoting FAIR and reproducible practices.

Nucleic acids research 2026-10-29 Medium

MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.

MitImpact 4 is a database that expands mitochondrial DNA variant interpretation from just the 13 protein-coding genes to the entire mitochondrial genome, covering all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants. This includes tRNA and rRNA genes, which harbor many pathogenic alleles but were previously a diagnostic blind spot because their effects depend on RNA structure rather than protein sequence. The resource provides functional annotations for coding and non-coding mtDNA variants, addressing a long-standing asymmetry in mitochondrial diagnostics.

Genomics & informatics 2026-10-28 Medium

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs under FDR control. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer analogy. This provides a resource for evaluating computational predictions of regulatory variants at GWAS loci.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification and metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. The system aims to streamline genome-guided natural product discovery by mapping genes to biosynthetic pathways.

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across tissues, individuals, and disease states. This reference-free approach reveals disease-relevant isoform changes that are missed by annotation-based methods.

Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.

SLCNV is a user-friendly Nextflow pipeline that automates chromosomal copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data, addressing the barrier that existing CNV tools pose for wet-lab biologists. It provides a flexible, streamlined workflow covering multiple copy number-related analyses, reducing the need for computational expertise.

Frontiers in microbiology 2026-01-01 Medium

cgMLST typing reproducibility is maintained across diverse whole-genome sequencing workflows in a multi-country HERA2 surveillance pilot.

This multi-country ring trial tested whether different laboratories' whole-genome sequencing workflows produce comparable core-genome MLST (cgMLST) typing results for bacterial surveillance. Six labs in four European countries sequenced a standardized panel of 25 isolates from five public health-relevant species, and cgMLST-based interpretations remained reproducible despite workflow differences. The findings support the robustness of cgMLST for routine cross-laboratory surveillance.

Survey of viruses associated with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in cucurbits in Georgia, United States.

This study surveyed the virome of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) collected from cucurbit crops in Tifton, Georgia, over two consecutive years using RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analysis. The work characterizes viruses associated with this major agricultural pest, which causes over $100 million in annual losses through plant virus transmission. The findings aim to inform understanding of vectoring potential and identify candidate viral biocontrol agents.

Genomic profiling and drug resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Indonesia: whole-genome sequencing of isolates from the 2017-2018 national Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey.

This study used whole-genome sequencing to characterize the genetic diversity, lineage distribution, and drug resistance mutations of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates collected during Indonesia's 2017–2018 national drug resistance survey. It provides a country-wide genomic snapshot of circulating lineages and resistance patterns across the Indonesian archipelago, supporting genotype-based surveillance of drug-resistant tuberculosis.

Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.

This paper describes the design and experimental validation of peptide binders targeting the nucleosome acidic patch using the BindCraft computational protein design pipeline. The authors demonstrate that de novo designed peptides can engage a key chromatin protein-protein interaction interface, suggesting a route toward engineered epigenetic modulators. The work bridges computational protein design with chromatin biology for potential therapeutic applications.

Assembly and comparative analysis of the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae), a tertiary relict plant endemic to China.

This study assembled and analyzed the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii, a rare Tertiary relict tree endemic to China. The genomic data were used to clarify phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae and to resolve the taxonomic placement and evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis. The work also provides molecular resources intended to support conservation and genetic breeding of this endangered species.
